news.headline: Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker III ruled out vs. Falcons
news.detail: Walker tweaked his groin and missed Friday's practice. CBS Sports and NBC Sports report the Chiefs ruled him out on Saturday (Nov. 14). Rookie Emmett Johnson is next in line, with Jaydn Ott questionable. Both Walker rushing picks (60+ and 100+ yards) look dead.

news.headline: Mahomes practiced fully; Kelce and Rice also on track
news.detail: Mahomes (knee/elbow) was a full participant all week, per Nov. 14 reports. NBC Sports says pain management could cut his throwing volume. Losing Walker may make Kansas City pass more.

news.headline: Watson cleared and starting for CLE; HOU defense thin
news.detail: Deshaun Watson cleared concussion protocol and starts for Cleveland. He is the NFL's most-sacked QB (33), facing a Houston defense that leads the league in sacks. Rookie WR Denzel Boston (toe) was expected to play. Houston has Danielle Hunter and Azeez Al-Shaair out, and Will Anderson Jr. is a concern. Vegas favors HOU by 4.5 and the model favors CLE, so this is a model-vs-Vegas split with no new…

news.headline: Cardinals start rookie Beck with a thin line and WR group; Rams lose Nacua
news.detail: Carson Beck makes his first start with center Hjalte Froholdt in concussion protocol, guards hurt and several receivers on IR. Rams WR Puka Nacua is on IR and OL Steve Avila is out. Matthew Stafford is healthy. Trey McBride is the clear focal point for Beck. The Rams are missing Nacua, which could cap the scoring.

news.headline: Seahawks' Lock starts hurt; Smith-Njigba is fully cleared
news.detail: Drew Lock was limited all week with elbow and oblique injuries but has no game designation and starts for Sam Darnold. Jaxon Smith-Njigba returned to full practice and is off the report. Leonard Williams is out. Las Vegas starts rookie Fernando Mendoza and its defense has allowed 30+ points six straight games.

news.headline: Bills RT Spencer Brown doubtful; Cook faces weak Jets run D
news.detail: Spencer Brown (ankle) is doubtful and Josh Allen was sacked four times last week. Jets rookie David Bailey has 7.5 sacks. James Cook ran 31 times for 107 yards last week against a Jets run defense ranked 26th, which helps his rushing picks. Garrett Wilson is expected back for the Jets.

news.headline: 49ers: Trent Williams and four CBs questionable; Evans out
news.detail: Trent Williams (shoulder) and CBs Renardo Green, Nate Hobbs, Deommodore Lenoir and Upton Stout are questionable. Mike Evans is out and Deebo Samuel is back. Dallas lists TE Jake Ferguson as questionable. Prescott and Purdy are not on the injury report. Weak San Francisco corners would help Lamb and Prescott's passing picks, and a missing Williams would hurt Purdy.

news.headline: Brissett makes first Ravens start; Herbert expected to play
news.detail: Jacoby Brissett was traded to Baltimore last week and starts after four days of practice, with Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley out. The Ravens haven't topped 13 points in four straight games. Justin Herbert's finger X-rays were negative and Jim Harbaugh said he will play. The Chargers are 0-8 and the Ravens are 4-5. The model likes Baltimore more than Vegas does (BAL -4.5).

news.headline: Bengals missing a few depth players; Burrow and Chase not listed
news.detail: Cincinnati ruled out S Kyle Dugger, CB Jalen Davis, WR Andrei Iosivas and G Brian Parker II. Burrow and Chase carry no designation. For Pittsburgh, DT Derrick Harmon (foot) is questionable and TE Pat Freiermuth was added with an illness. Burrow has 2,386 yards and 23 TDs this season.

NFL.recap: Weeks 9 and 10 went well on winners: 14 of 16 graded games picked the right winner (misses were GB over NE and WAS over NYG). Against the spread it was 7-9, because the model kept being off in blowouts like JAX over BAL, HOU over LAC and BUF over MIN, where turnovers and efficiency swung the games. Totals went 10-4, with the over/under right in most games.

lessons.lesson: When the model picks a different winner than the Vegas favorite, its side wins about as often as Vegas's chances say, which is less than half the time.
lessons.evidence: 2 of 7 graded games this season where the model's side was not the Vegas favorite won. Past-season test: the model's side won 47.4% in 2010-2019 (Vegas 42.9%) and 42.9% in 2020-2025 (Vegas 43.3%), so no edge over Vegas's own chances. HOU at CLE is this week's case, and news (Watson back, Houston's strong pass rush) does not favor the model's side.
lessons.test: Check results of the attached check on 2010-2019 and 2020-2025 against Vegas's chances; add up this season's cases until there are 20+.

test_result.note: Won 43% in 2020–2025 when Vegas's chances said 43%, about what Vegas's own chances said, so there's no edge.

lessons.lesson: Large gaps between the model's total and Vegas's total have not paid off.
lessons.evidence: Past-season test says the model's side with a 4+ point gap won 48.3% in 2020-2025 (174 games, 4 pushes), below break-even; no 2010-2019 data. This season, the over/under is 30-24 overall and went 10-4 in the last two weeks, so the small sample does not show the same weakness. This week's LA at ARI (gap 6.3) and KC at ATL (gap 3.6) are big-gap or near-big-gap games.
lessons.test: Compare gap groups under 2, 2-4 and 4+ on past seasons; keep tracking this season's 4+ gap games until 20+.

test_result.note: Won 48.3% in 2020–2025; it needs about 54.5% to beat the 52.4% break-even with room to spare.

lessons.lesson: Many big misses come from efficiency swings, which the model can't see before kickoff.
lessons.evidence: 9 of the 16 games where the winner was wrong through Week 9 named efficiency as the main reason (the WAS-NYG miss had no named driver). Newest misses: JAX-BAL off by 17.5 and HOU-LAC by 18.1, with no stat explaining most of it; BUF-MIN was off 15.7 mostly on efficiency and turnovers.
lessons.test: On past seasons, measure how often big spread misses (over 8 points) are driven by efficiency versus turnovers. Check whether the model's misses are larger than Vegas's overall.

lessons.lesson: Long-shot picks (underdog winners and big-game props) hit a bit below the model's chances and lose units.
lessons.evidence: Underdog picks are 5 of 19 against 7.7 expected (-6.54 units). Big-game picks are 12 of 36 against 11.8 expected (-8.99 units), so the loss is mostly from prices. Milestone picks are 31 of 40 against 29.9 expected (-3.29 units).
lessons.test: On past seasons, compare predicted chance with actual hit rate for underdog winners and long-shot props in buckets of model chance. Also check whether prices paid are shorter than fair odds. Needs 20+ picks per bucket.

lessons.lesson: Best-value picks against the sportsbook are running a little below the model's chances.
lessons.evidence: 12 of 24 best-value picks hit this season, against 12.7 expected, at -1.09 units. The gap is under 1 hit. This week's five value picks sit only 0.1 to 1.5 points over break-even.
lessons.test: On past seasons, check hit rate of the model's top value picks by size of edge. Needs 20+ picks per edge group.

lessons.lesson: The model's margin errors are larger than Vegas's, and it is below .500 against the spread.
lessons.evidence: Average spread miss is 9.7 for the model vs 9.0 for Vegas over 56 graded games; the model is 25-31-1 against the spread (7-9 in the last two weeks). Past-season test of the model's spread side: 51.9% in 2010-2019 and 48.9% in 2020-2025 across 1,660 games. That is below the 52.4% break-even, so no edge.
lessons.test: Compare average absolute margin error with Vegas's, by week and season, before changing anything.

test_result.note: Won 48.9% in 2020–2025; it needs about 54.5% to beat the 52.4% break-even with room to spare.

lessons.lesson: Big gaps between the model and Vegas on games with a QB change are not clearly misses by the model.
lessons.evidence: Earlier cases: DAL at PHI, PHI at WAS (Hurts on IR) and MIN (Murray out, Wentz in). Past-season test of the model's spread side with a QB change and a 3+ point gap: 54.2% in 2010-2019 (203 games) and 54.4% in 2020-2025 (160 games). That is above break-even but short of the 54.5% needed to count as an edge. This week BAL (Brissett), ARI (Beck), MIA (McCord), SEA (Lock), LV (Mendoza) and CLE (Watso…
lessons.test: Track this season's cases until 20+; compare the model's margin error in QB-change games with all others.

test_result.note: Won 54.4% in 2020–2025; it needs about 54.5% to beat the 52.4% break-even with room to spare.

lessons.lesson: Player-prop picks can be spoiled by late inactives that the model does not see.
lessons.evidence: 1 case this week: Kenneth Walker III (L19, L27) was ruled out Saturday after the lists were made. Milestone picks are otherwise 31 of 40 against 29.9 expected, so the effect is small so far.
lessons.test: Track how many graded milestone picks lose because the player did not play, until 20+ cases; compare with the hit rate of picks where the player played.

news.headline: Rain and cold in Norman; Ole Miss thin at RB and on the line
news.detail: Nov 15 forecasts call for steady rain, a high near 43 and east wind of 10-15 mph in Norman, and News 9 says the game is being played Sunday in the rain. Ole Miss is also without RB Kewan Lacy and starting RG Patrick Kutas. Both things lean toward fewer points, which fits the Under.

news.headline: Ole Miss QB Chambliss cleared, but 11 Rebels are out
news.detail: Trinidad Chambliss was dropped from the SEC availability report on Thursday (Nov 12), so he looks set to start. Ole Miss still has 11 players out, including RB Kewan Lacy, OL Patrick Kutas and LB Keaton Thomas, and RB Makhi Frazier was questionable. Oklahoma lists absences too (LB Taylor Heim, DB Dakota Fields, WR Trell Harris, TE Trynae Washington, OL Fred Hinton). The model picks Ole Miss and V…

item_notes.College|value|401856887|total|under|||48: The model's own chance for the Under is 50.6%, below the 52.4% needed, but rain, cold and Ole Miss missing its top RB and a starting lineman point toward a lower-scoring game.

College.recap: Week 11 went well for picking winners and badly for margins and totals. The model had the right winner in 28 of the 40 results shown, but it was about 18-20-1 against the spread and only 12-27 on totals, because the games mostly ran under the model's higher totals. Big misses were led by efficiency, then turnovers: South Carolina, Cal and Arkansas State all lost the turnover battle badly. Upsets like Georgia Tech over Clemson, UNLV over New Mexico and Arkansas over South Carolina hurt most.

lessons.lesson: The 'model total above Vegas means the over hits' pattern does not hold up. The model's totals picks have lost more than they won, and Vegas totals have mostly been too high lately.
lessons.evidence: Season totals record is 127-166 (43%). In the 40 Week 11 results shown, the model's totals side went about 12-27 (one no pick), and the under hit in about 27 of 39. The built-in test shows the model's side won only 50.7-51.4% in 2020-2025.
lessons.test: On past seasons, group games by model total minus Vegas total (0-3, 3-6, 6+) and check how often the over hits in each group, by week. Also compare the model's and Vegas's average total error. Need 20+ games per group.

test_result.note: Won 51.4% in 2020–2025; it needs about 54.5% to beat the 52.4% break-even with room to spare.

lessons.lesson: Late-season unders have hit much more often than Vegas totals imply.
lessons.evidence: In the 39 Week 11 results shown with a total pick, the under hit in about 27 (69%). That is one week of games, so the results are correlated and it may be luck or weather. Not yet shown over a longer span.
lessons.test: On past seasons, check how often the under hits in Weeks 10 and later, by total line. Compare with earlier weeks. Need 20+ games per group.

test_result.note: Won 49.6% in 2020–2025; it needs about 54.5% to beat the 52.4% break-even with room to spare.

lessons.lesson: Big misses are spread across several causes, but efficiency still leads, with turnovers next.
lessons.evidence: Week 11, 26 of the 40 results shown missed by 8+ points: efficiency first in 14, turnovers 6, finishing drives 4, big plays 1, nothing stood out 1. Week 10 had efficiency first in 14 of 26. Efficiency is measured after the game, so it partly restates the miss.
lessons.test: On past seasons, check whether a team's success rate in prior games predicts the model's error next game. Also compare turnover margin and points per trip inside the 40 with long-run averages, to see if misses lean one way or are random.

lessons.lesson: When the model picks a different winner than Vegas, this season has gone badly, but past seasons say the model's side holds up.
lessons.evidence: This season about 5 of 18 right. Week 11 added App State over Marshall, Coastal Carolina over Arkansas State and Syracuse over NC State to Vegas, and UAB over Temple to the model (1 of 4). The Arizona State at UCF result was not in the data shown. Built-in test: the model's side won 47% in 2020-2025 against Vegas's 41% (379 games).
lessons.test: On past seasons, list games where the model and Vegas disagree on the winner, then compare the model's win rate with Vegas's. Need 20+ games.

test_result.note: Won 47% in 2020–2025 when Vegas's chances said 41%. Those chances have the bookmaker's cut removed; a real bet pays it, which eats a couple of points of that edge.

lessons.lesson: The 'Best value against the sportsbook' list has been weak.
lessons.evidence: Season: 14 of 35 hit against 17.8 expected, at -8.27 units. Edges are thin (about 51% against 52.4% needed), so the model's own chance is below break-even on the Ole Miss at Oklahoma Under too.
lessons.test: On past seasons, bucket the model's spread and total picks by edge size and compare hit rates with the 52.4% break-even. Need 20+ games per bucket.

lessons.lesson: Underdog picks have hit about as often as the model expected, and long prices have kept units positive.
lessons.evidence: Season: 14 of 34 hit against 13.7 expected, at +6.53 units. A few hits swing the units a lot, so there is much luck in this list.
lessons.test: On past seasons, compare predicted chance with actual win rate for the model's underdog picks, in buckets of model chance (under 35%, 35-45%, 45%+). Need 20+ picks per bucket.

lessons.lesson: The 'Most likely winners' list has landed close to the model's own chances.
lessons.evidence: Season: 28 of 30 hit against 27.1 expected, at +0.97 units. Prices are very short, so one miss costs a lot.
lessons.test: On past seasons, bucket the model's top win chances (90%+, 85-90%) and compare with actual win rate and with Vegas's no-vig chance. Need 20+ games per bucket.

lessons.lesson: The model's spread misses are slightly larger than Vegas's, and favorites have not covered reliably in November.
lessons.evidence: Season (300 games): average spread miss 12.8 for the model against 12.2 for Vegas. Winners right 199 of 300 (66%), spread 138-153-5. In the 40 Week 11 results shown the model was about 18-20-1 against the spread. The earlier idea that favorites cover more in November did not hold up in the built-in test (50.4% in 2020-2025).
lessons.test: On past seasons, compare the model's and Vegas's average spread error. Then test whether averaging the model's margin and Vegas's margin beats either alone, and whether the gap changes by week of season.

test_result.note: Won 50.4% in 2020–2025; it needs about 54.5% to beat the 52.4% break-even with room to spare.
